note:
Coverage. All 28 physical pages were read at text level and all 39 measured regions were inspected on a crop: the eleven figure-bearing pages (p4, p7, p8, p9, p11, p16, p17, p19, p20, p21, p22), the table pages (p18, p20, p22) and every equation region the clustering pass mistook for artwork (p5, p10, p11, p12, p13, p15, p16). Eighteen exhibits are printed in this paper and all eighteen are measured regions, so there is no declared gap: thirteen figures, five tables, twenty-one exclusions. The exclusions split as ten not-an-exhibit (nine pasted display equations plus the acronym glossary block on p5), five duplicates and six fragments. Two of those mechanisms are new to this lane and both are worth naming because they will recur. First, the layout pass boxes ONE drawing TWICE with overlapping crops: Figure 4 is captured once as a vector and once as a raster over the same coordinates, and all four panels of Figure 8 are captured twice each, so eight regions belong to four drawings. Second, one region can hold TWO side-by-side drawings: the K-Means panels on p19 and the Impact panels on p19 are each two drawings in one box, and the choropleths of Figure 13 are two regions of one exhibit. The convention is the same as every split exhibit in this block - the anchor is a measured region, the recorded area is the union - and on this paper the difference is large: Figure 8's anchor reports 0.118 of the page and its union is 0.225, Figure 13's anchor reports 0.052 against a union of 0.107. 

The caption system, which is this paper's one genuinely consistent habit. Eighteen exhibits, eighteen captions, and every single one is printed BELOW its exhibit - thirteen figures under their art, five tables under their grid, no exception anywhere in 28 pages. That is the inverse of the block's booktabs papers, and it is a real authoring discipline rather than a rendering accident: the tables' captions are below even though the text layer reads the caption FIRST and the grid after it, which is also true of Figure 12 and is the trap this lane has to keep flagging - reading order is not caption side. The form is 'Figure <n>:' and 'Table <n>:' with a colon, sentence case, and one sentence each; two captions drop the terminal period and run into the body text ('Figure 11: WFSI and CCIC for Greece from 2008 to 2012 The details for each year...'). All eighteen are noun phrases, none states a unit, none states a condition, none draws a conclusion - but unlike a bare-label convention eight of the eighteen DO name the quantity plotted (CCI, WFSI, CCIC, or the pair), which is more caption information than the last three papers in this lane carry combined. 

Numbering and citation. Every exhibit is named by number at least once - there is no positional-only pointer and no under-cited exhibit - and sixteen of eighteen are pointed at on their own page or one page before. Two exceptions carry the meaning. Figure 3 is named on p6 and printed on p8, because the four-category split is described in the method paragraph before the wheel exists. Figure 7 is the reverse: the art prints on p16 under an unnumbered teaser paragraph and the paper does not name it until p17, so its lead_pages is negative and it is the one exhibit in the paper whose first numbered pointer comes after its own page. Against that, the paper's worst structural defect is not a citation gap but a section misplacement: Table 5, the Sudan intervention cost table, belongs to 10 Task 4 on p21 and is printed on p22 under the by-then-current heading 11 Task 5, so the table appears after the section that supersedes it. 

Charts. Thirteen figures split cleanly by job: five schematics or wheels in Introduction and Model (the only flowchart-or-schematic pair, the only node-link pair, the one composite and two radial charts the vocabulary has no word for), and eight computed plots after section 6. The paper never draws a histogram, a box, a heatmap, a photo, a surface or a table-as-figure; six of the fourteen vocabulary families go unused. Panels are the norm - eight of thirteen are multipanel, two of those at the five-panel ceiling and three at exactly four panels - and NOT ONE multipanel grid shares its axes. Figure 8 is the demonstration: four y windows (0.10-0.80, 0.20-0.80, 0.10-0.90, 0.15-0.70), two tick steps, a fourth box visibly narrower than its neighbours, and a legend key order that ROTATES panel by panel, so red means Social in one box and Economic in the next. Figure 10 does the same thing with two y windows (0-35% beside 0-45%), which is exactly the figure the Sudan argument rests on. THE HABIT THAT COSTS THE ARGUMENT. Against that, one exhibit is honest to the point of being the best in the paper - Figure 10 prints its bin edges ('<=0.129' ... '>0.849'), its percentage ticks with signs, and a legend below each panel - and one argues against itself: Figure 13 panel (b) is captioned 'Weighted Fragile Continent Index' and shaded country by country, and the very next sentences admit the reading fails ('please find Australia in both graphs... The modeling result is not very ideal'). Colour is the paper's blind spot: a colourbar appears exactly once, on Figure 13's maps, while the sunburst's outer ring (Figure 2) and the WFSI wheel's four quadrant gradients (Figure 3) shade a value that no key, legend or colourbar anywhere on the page decodes. The only 3-D is Figure 9's four perspective scatter boxes - a 2-D page's answer to 'four dimensions cannot be shown in one figure'. Legends go inside the axes when they exist at all (four of five), never above. The smallest type in the paper is Figure 11's radar spokes and rings at about 5 pt. 

Tables. Five grids, five measured regions, and every one is set to the text measure rather than to its content: three sit on the 339 pt column (x 128.5 to 467.7), Table 4 runs 358 pt and Table 3 breaks the margin at 405 pt, all portrait, none rotated, none continued across a page break. Dressing splits three ways: Tables 1 and 2 are closed frames with a full internal grid and a lavender label band over the header and stub; Tables 3 and 4 are booktabs, horizontal rules only; Table 5 is open-sided with a full horizontal grid, three internal verticals and the paper's only zebra shading. No table merges a cell, prints a diagonal header, puts a unit in a header or aligns its decimals, although four of the five print four or five decimal places on every numeric column - so a reader comparing 0.8294 against 0.26598 has to count digits by eye. Row and column counts track named objects rather than numbers: 4 columns for a three-metric summary, 11 for four node pairs, 7 and 6 for five years, 8 rows for six interventions plus a total row. The defects are content defects rather than form defects. Table 4's caption reads 'WFSI C', the variable name truncated and the CCIC column that Table 3 carries simply absent, so the caption's promise and the grid disagree. Table 5 welds every cost to its unit inside a body cell ('$8 million/year', '$14.18million/year'), which makes the cost column a string that cannot be summed - and the closing note sentence welds the same way. Table 2 is introduced only as 'Ta- ble 2', hyphenated across a line break, the one exhibit in the paper whose first mention is not printable as a single string. 

Apparatus. The folio is wrong at the very end: 'Page 24 of 24' runs through physical p27 and the last page prints 'Page 25 of 24', so the document claims one page more than it has. Spacing welds recur through the whole paper - 'Climate Change Indexby Country', 'theweak cluster', 'trainednetwork' - and they land inside exhibit text as well as prose: the panel titles of Figure 13 print 'Indexby Country'. One identical red Chinese resale banner is stamped on EVERY page of the document and is absent from the text layer entirely, which is why the layout pass never sees it and why a text-only pass would report this paper as clean. Figure 7 is pasted over the body column so a line of prose runs under its x axis, and Figure 2's caption is set INLINE inside a justified paragraph - the only exhibit in 28 pages whose caption has no line of its own, with body text running through the left band of the artwork.
rules: Every one of the thirteen figure captions is printed BELOW its art and every one of the five table captions is printed below its grid - 18 of 18 below, no exception in 28 pages [caption.position].

Caption position and reading order are not the same thing: Figure 12's caption is geometrically under the plot while the text layer lists it before the axes, and Figure 11's caption runs straight into the body sentence with no terminal period, so a caption-side rule read off the text layer alone would be wrong [caption.position].

The caption form is `Figure <n>: <noun phrase>` with a colon, sentence case and no terminal verb, and the tables use the identical form - 'Table 3: WFSI and CCIC for Greece from 2008 to 2012.' - so caption style does not separate a grid from a chart [caption.numbering].

Captions stay short - four to eleven words, one sentence each - but unlike a bare-label convention eight of the eighteen name the quantity plotted: CCI, WFSI, CCIC or the pair 'WFSI and CCIC' [caption.variable_count].

Not one of the eighteen captions states a unit, a parameter condition or a conclusion, and not one is written as a sentence in either voice: the paper labels, it does not read its own exhibits [caption.concludes].
One caption is broken: 'Table 4: WFSI C for Greece from 2013 to 2017' truncates the variable name that Table 3 printed in full [caption.verbatim].

Ten of the eighteen pointers use the as-shown-in formula, five name the exhibit directly, two wrap it in a parenthetical and one has no lead sentence at all - Figure 1 is left to explain itself and is read only afterwards, on the page that follows it [mention.lead_pattern].

Pointing usually happens on or one page before the art: sixteen of eighteen are named on their own page or one page earlier, Figure 3 is named two pages early because the method is described before the wheel exists, and Figure 7 is the one backward case where lead_pages is negative [mention.lead_pages].

Most exhibits are named once and never again: fifteen of eighteen carry count 1, and the three that carry 2 are the three the argument returns to - the framework figure on p4, the Bayesian network on p11 and the prediction table on p20, whose forecast is re-read on p21 [mention.count].

The pointer sentence carries the only scale the reader gets: 'we set the radar chart boundary to 0.35' and 'the gray area means that we have no data of it' are printed in prose and never inside the exhibit [mention.trail_sentence].

Families split by job, not by taste: the six figures in Introduction and Model are schematics, networks and wheels (flowchart-or-schematic twice, node-link-network twice, one composite and one sunburst filed as 'other'), and every figure after section 6 is a computed plot - line twice, scatter twice, bar once, radar once, map once [geometry.family].

The paper never draws a histogram, a box plot, a heatmap, a photographic plate, a surface or a table-as-figure: six of the fourteen vocabulary families go unused across thirteen figures [geometry.family].
Composite-panel appears exactly once, as a four-quadrant wheel with four satellite donuts (1+4), and it is the paper's substitute for the 12-number table it never prints [geometry.panel_count].

Eight of thirteen figures are multipanel - two at the five-panel ceiling (the WFSI composite and the five-year radar sheet), three at four panels, two at three and one at two - so the paper thinks in panels even where a single plot would carry the point [geometry.panel_count].

No multipanel figure declares shared axes, and the two 2x2 grids prove it: Figure 8's four panels run on y windows of 0.10-0.80, 0.20-0.80, 0.10-0.90 and 0.15-0.70 with two different tick steps, Figure 10's run 0-35% and 0-45%. A grid of separately produced images is the house pattern [geometry.shared_axes].
The legend goes inside the axes or not at all: of the five figures that carry a legend, four set it inside the plot area and only Figure 10 puts its key below, once per panel [geometry.legend].

A colourbar appears once in thirteen figures, on the two choropleths of Figure 13; the sunburst's outer ring and the WFSI wheel's four quadrant gradients shade a value with no key, so two exhibits encode meaning the page never decodes [geometry.colorbar].

Three-dimensional artwork appears once, Figure 9, and it is four perspective scatter boxes rather than a surface or a mesh - the paper's answer to 'four dimensions cannot be shown in one figure' is four 3-D boxes on a 2-D page [geometry.three_d].

Printed numbers are the norm for plots and absent from diagrams: the two flowcharts, the sunburst, the WFSI wheel and the four 3-D box panels carry no tick numbers at all, while all five 2-D plots and the radar sheet print them [geometry.printed_numbers].

Table dressing splits three ways: two tables are closed frames with a full internal grid (Tables 1 and 2), two are booktabs with horizontal rules only (Tables 3 and 4), and one is open-sided with a full horizontal grid and three internal verticals (Table 5) [table.rule_style].
Zebra shading is used once, on Table 5. The lavender band on Tables 1 and 2 marks the header and stub cells, not alternate rows, and must not be read as zebra [table.zebra].

Merged cells, diagonal headers and units-in-header never occur: 0 of 5 tables on all three fields, even where the numbers are percentages in one column and raw counts in the next [table.merged_cells].

No table is decimal-aligned even though four of the five print four or five decimal places on every numeric column: the values are centred, so a reader comparing 0.8294 against 0.26598 has to count the digits [table.decimal_aligned].

Every table is set to the text measure rather than to its content: three sit on the 339 pt column (x 128.5 to 467.7), Table 4 runs 358 pt and Table 3 breaks the margin at 405 pt, so width is a constant here and never a response to the number of columns [table.width].
Orientation is portrait in all five tables; the paper never turns a table sideways and never continues one across a page break [table.orientation].

Table size tracks the number of named objects, not the number of numbers: 4 columns for a three-metric summary, 11 for four node pairs, 7 and 6 for five years each, 8 rows for six interventions plus a total row [table.rows].

Only one of the five tables carries a note sentence, and it is the one whose numbers are welded to their units - '$14.18million/year' printed inside a body cell so the cost column cannot be summed [table.note_sentence].

Placement follows the paragraph that needs the exhibit, and the two exceptions are instructive: Figure 3 is printed two pages after its own pointer, and Table 5 is printed on p22 under 11 Task 5 although its pointer and its argument belong to 10 Task 4 on p21 [place.section_path].

Model sections get diagrams and result sections get plots, with no crossover: all six schematic, network and wheel figures sit under 1.2, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, and all seven computed plots and all five tables sit under 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 8, 9.1, 9.2 and 11 [place.section_kind].

No exhibit is placed in the summary, the assumptions, the data sections or the appendix: seven exhibit-free pages run between page 4 and page 16, and all five tables sit in the paper's last eleven pages [place.doc_order].

Exhibits share pages in pairs, and once in a triple: p11, p18, p19, p22 carry two each and p20 carries three (Figure 11 and both Greek tables), each group read in one paragraph, so the page is the unit of argument, not the exhibit [place.page_order].

No exhibit owns a page and none is full-bleed: the largest single-anchor exhibit is Table 5 at 0.174 of the page, and the largest recorded area is Figure 8's union at 0.225 against a 0.118 anchor, because the pass boxed its four panels twice over [place.area_frac].

Every exhibit sits under a numbered heading, and the number itself is load-bearing here: the two case studies are the only sections that receive both a figure and a table, and their tables are the only ones whose rows are dates [place.section_numbered].
